cards.explanation: The title is King of the Jews, friends. Pilate, the Roman governor, asks Jesus, "Are You the King of the Jews?" (Matthew 27:11). Jesus answers, "You have said so…" Pilate asks a yes or no question and gets a short answer back.

The answer is False. Jesus doesn't argue back. The text says that when He was accused by the chief priests and elders, "…He gave no answer." (Matthew 27:12). Picture accusations coming from the chief priests and elders, and Jesus giving no answer. I can't even stay quiet when the oven timer beeps.

The governor is amazed, friends. Jesus gave no answer, "…not even to a single charge, much to the governor’s amazement." (Matthew 27:14). Pilate had just asked if He heard how many charges there were (Matthew 27:13). I think he expected some kind of defense, and he got silence instead.

The word is prisoner. "Now it was the governor’s custom at the feast to release to the crowd a prisoner of their choosing." (Matthew 27:15). The crowd gets to pick. That one custom is about to matter a whole lot.

The reason is envy, friends. "For he knew it was out of envy that they had handed Jesus over to him." (Matthew 27:18). Pilate saw what was behind it. The text gives us his read on the situation, and it was envy.

She tells him to have nothing to do with that innocent man, friends. Pilate's wife sends this message: "Have nothing to do with that innocent man…" (Matthew 27:19). She calls Jesus innocent, and the message reaches Pilate while he is sitting on the judgment seat. Her words say it loud and clear.

The answer is True. Pilate's wife's message says, "…for I have suffered terribly in a dream today because of Him." (Matthew 27:19). The text doesn't tell us what the dream was. I think it shook her up. I'd be sending that message too.

They ask for Barabbas to be freed and Jesus put to death, friends. "…the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus put to death." (Matthew 27:20). They worked the crowds, and the crowds asked. Heavy stuff, and it's right there in the text.
The word is Crucify, friends. When Pilate asks what to do with Jesus, "They all answered, 'Crucify Him!'" (Matthew 27:22). Two words, and they all said them. This is a heavy part of the story.

The answer is False. Pilate asks, "What evil has He done?" and the crowd "shouted all the louder, 'Crucify Him!'" (Matthew 27:23). They don't answer his question. They get louder. It's a heavy moment, and the text doesn't soften it.

Pilate washes his hands with water, friends. He "…took water and washed his hands before the crowd." (Matthew 27:24). Then he says, "I am innocent of this man’s blood…" Washing up in front of everybody is a loud move, and I think he wanted the crowd to see it.

The words are innocent and responsibility, friends. Pilate says, "I am innocent of this man’s blood…" (Matthew 27:24). He says it while washing his hands in front of the crowd. Innocent is the word he picks for himself. Then he tells the crowd, "You bear the responsibility." (Matthew 27:24). He's handing the weight to them.

Pilate has Jesus flogged, friends. "But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified." (Matthew 27:26). Pilate releases Barabbas, and Jesus is flogged. It's a heavy verse, and I think it's worth slowing down on.
